title: Sri Lanka’s welfare registry dropped 331,653 names and added 153,511 after a nationwide re‑certification.
body_paragraphs: The updated rolls now list 991,800 people eligible for cash transfers across the two lowest‑income bands, with payments scheduled to start on 27 November. Lists were displayed at local offices with a 10‑day window for objections before divisional committees review cases.

The exercise followed criticism of leakage when over 3.12 million self‑declarations were filed last year, and it comes as transitional categories ended in 2025–26 to contain costs. Officials said a second tranche of revisions would follow, aiming to focus benefits more tightly while preserving fiscal room in a programme central to social stability.
bold_phrases: payments scheduled to start on 27 November

title: The central bank warned inflation could rise if oil stays around $100 a barrel for longer.
body_paragraphs: Consumer prices rose 8.1 percent year‑on‑year in September, the highest in 40 months, after domestic fuel was priced to reflect global markets. Authorities said they would avoid using interest rates to chase supply‑side shocks unless demand pressures built.

The state fuel supplier has lifted pump prices by roughly half since the Middle East conflict began, increasing pass‑through to transport and power. Policymakers said earlier forecasts assumed crude drifting to about $90 by year‑end, a path that now looks less certain.
bold_phrases: lifted pump prices by roughly half

title: The cabinet approved a $100 million Asian Development Bank loan for a macro‑recovery programme.
body_paragraphs: Half the financing is policy‑based and half is for investments through the lender’s ordinary capital resources (the ADB’s main, non‑concessional window). The package forms part of a wider $620 million envelope negotiated to support reforms aligned with the IMF’s Extended Fund Facility (an upper‑credit‑tranche programme that anchors fiscal and structural conditions).

Officials said loan talks had concluded and signing would follow internal processes. A related infrastructure push under the Mahaweli water scheme secured a $60 million OPEC Fund facility, and authorities tied both packages to resilience and inclusion goals.

title: Police suspended senior officers and the bar demanded an impartial probe after a custodial death in Homagama.
body_paragraphs: Three officers were removed from duty first, followed by the arrest of the crimes division head and suspension of the station chief. The courts ordered a post‑mortem and preliminary inquiries, while an independent professional body cited constitutional guarantees on life and due process.

The case drew scrutiny as medical findings pointed to multiple injuries, and prosecutors were urged to preserve evidence. The human‑rights community said accountability would test longstanding pledges to end abuse in detention.
bold_phrases: arrest of the crimes division head

title: Sri Lanka set performance‑based frameworks for state‑enterprise collective agreements from 2027.
body_paragraphs: An expert committee aligned workplace pacts with industrial, trade union and shop‑and‑office laws, adding profit‑sharing and bonus guidelines. Existing deals remain in force through 2026 to allow transition.

title: Customs said October revenue hit 152.8 billion rupees by the 21st day, surpassing 79 percent of the month’s target.
body_paragraphs: Collections exceeded the annual goal by 103.6 percent with stronger enforcement and a rebound in imports after prior controls. Last year’s take rose 64.2 percent to 2.55 trillion rupees, lifting the department to a top‑tier role in meeting IMF‑linked fiscal targets.

title: Rights groups said the organised‑crime bill risked replicating abusive anti‑terror provisions.
body_paragraphs: Critics flagged detention orders of up to a year with limited judicial oversight and admissibility of police‑taken confessions, echoing past practices under the PTA (Prevention of Terrorism Act, a 1979 law widely criticised for arbitrary detention and torture). They also warned of broad surveillance powers without court orders to obtain telecom and location data.
bold_phrases: detention orders of up to a year

title: Japan pledged over 600 million rupees to build a Kelani River water‑quality data platform through 2030.
body_paragraphs: The programme equips regulators and universities to monitor a basin that supplies drinking water to Colombo and hosts over 5,400 industries. Partners cited missing groundwater standards and climate risks as barriers to cleaner supply.

title: The navy and coast guard seized 561.7 kg of heroin and crystal meth on a Matara beach in a joint operation.
body_paragraphs: The haul, packed in sacks and travel bags beside a dinghy, carried an estimated street value above 11.8 billion rupees. Investigators said combined maritime operations in the past year had netted narcotics worth about 97 billion rupees.

title: Online appointments became mandatory for passport applicants at five regional offices from 29 October.
body_paragraphs: The booking system covers one‑day and normal services at centres in Matara, Kandy, Kurunegala, Vavuniya and Jaffna, with family slots capped at two adults and three children. Urgent cases may still use the head office without prior booking.
bold_phrases: Matara, Kandy, Kurunegala, Vavuniya and Jaffna
family slots capped at two adults and three children
